Hearing. The State Highway Commission then certified to the Federal Highway Administration that no requests in response to the notice were recieved and that no further hearings would be required.
On November 13, 1970, the Federal Highway Administration after careful review of the Airport Spur's Design Study Report and preliminary plan designs gave design approval for the proposed highway facility. With approval, Milwaukee County engaged engineering consultants to prepare design plans for the Airport Spur. The design plans were for an alignment within the recommended Corridor #5. The project design was monitored for items recognized at that time as being of environmental concern.
Under the provisions of Section 5c of the FHWA Guidelines for Implementation of Section 102(2)(C) of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, the project was assessed by FHWA on February 10, 1971 to determine the necessity of an environmental impact statement. It was determined that the project development and highway plans did incorporate, to the extent practical, those feature, necessary to minimize harm to the quality of the human environment; that an environmental statement would not be required; and that the project could proceed in a normal manner. This written environmental assessment re-evaluation of the proposed project was approved by the Federal Highway Administration on February 22, 1971 and re-affirmed on October 4, 1972.
